"I would first establish the first day of the patient's last menstrual period and assess whether it was a normal period and whether her cycles are regular. I would calculate the initial EDD using the LMP, assuming a 28-day cycle. I would then review any early ultrasound, particularly the crown-rump length in the first trimester, as this provides an accurate assessment of gestational age. If there is a clinically significant discrepancy between the LMP and ultrasound dating, I would assess the reliability of the LMP and apply the relevant dating guideline to determine whether the EDD should be revised. Once an EDD has been reliably established, I would avoid changing it simply because later fetal measurements suggest a smaller or larger gestational age."
